messages:
mara: Heads-up — ran into a reproducer where a client reconnect + early-EoF leads to a duplicated tool-call charge. Short summary: client opens streaming session, sends a partial prompt then disconnects. Router falls back to a tool-call path on reconnect, server completes the stream and charges a provisional streaming token. When the client reconnects a second time the tool-call executes again and we end up confirming the same logical work twice.

sam: ugh. any idempotency token on the client side?

mara: nope — this is our mobile SDK behavior. session_id exists but we don't derive an idempotency key for midstream toolcalls. logs attached (snippet):

mara: ```
INFO router: session=abc123 trace=tx-9 recv: client disconnect (partial)
WARN router: session=abc123 fallback->toolcall route chosen
INFO tool-runner: req_id=tr-77 provisional_charge=12 tokens trace=tx-9
INFO billing-ledger: provisional_record id=prv-555 trace=tx-9

# later on reconnect
INFO router: session=abc123 reconnect start trace=tx-17
INFO tool-runner: req_id=tr-77 replayed, confirmed_charge=12 trace=tx-17
ERROR billing: duplicate_confirm prr-555 vs prr-556
```

izzy: are tr-77 / prr-555 globally unique? looks like the tool-runner reused a request id across retries which makes the ledger think it's a new confirmation.

mara: yep — tool-runner used a monotonic per-instance counter so when the process restarted the id namespace overlapped. combined with the lack of client idempotency and router provisional-confirm handshake we double-count.

sam: quick mitigation ideas: (1) router should attach a deterministic idempotency token derived from session_id + prompt_hash; (2) ledger should treat provisional->confirmed transitions idempotently using a trace_id window; (3) console should show provisional vs confirmed amounts and surface quick refunds.

izzy: +1 on (1). Also we should emit explicit telemetry events so a single trace can show provisional_charge, provisional_claim, confirmed_charge, and refunds. Metric names proposed: redwood.billing.provisional.tokens, redwood.billing.confirmed.tokens, redwood.billing.provisional-to-confirmed.ratio.

mara: for reproability I'll add a small harness that replays disconnects at different points (EOF before toolcall, EOF during toolcall). I think the truncation path is important — sometimes we truncate the user prompt on reconnect which changes the prompt_hash and makes dedupe fail.

sam: good catch. So the idempotency derivation needs to use stable inputs: session_id + initial_prompt_prefix_hash + tool_name. If prompt gets truncated on retry we still map to same id.

izzy: console UX idea: when a provisional charge exists show it inline on the session timeline with a "provisional" badge and a link to the trace. Allow refunds with a one-click button that opens a prefilled ticket (refund reason + trace id). That will speed ops investigations.

mara: one more nuance — our current provisional TTL is 2m; if tool-runner confirms across boundaries (e.g., provisional recorded in router but confirmed by a downstream runner) the ledger may receive two distinct confirm messages. We should add a confirm-dedup key computed as sha256(trace_id + provisional_id) and have the ledger ignore duplicate confirms if the underlying tokens and trace match.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: billing-ledger v2.1.4 -> canary at 1704517200, rollout 10% for 15m.

sam: next steps: i'll sketch a small RFC with these changes: router-idempotency, stable id derivation, ledger confirm-dedupe, telemetry events, and console provisional UX. Aim for implementation plan + canary playbook.

mara: thanks — i'll drop the reproducer and logs into the RFC and add the harness scripts.

izzy: also add dashboards: provisional/confirmed per route, % of provisional never confirmed after TTL, top sessions by provisional tokens. Those will help catch regressions fast.

mara: ok wrapping up — i'll create the RFC and tag y'all. If anyone wants the raw logs now ping me and i'll share the sanitizer'd dump. :thumbsup:
